#### What this PR does / why we need it:
This PR extracts ParseError from PodInfo, makes NewPodInfo adopt to golang traditional style by doing the following things:

1. Extract ParseError from PodInfo.
2. Return error in `NewpodInfo` and some other related functions.
3. Change how these functions are called.
     - for test files, I created corresponding `mustNewxxx` function, which calls the original function  and raise a panic when error occured.
     ```
      func mustNewPodInfo(t *testing.T, pod *v1.Pod) *framework.PodInfo {
	      t.Helper()
	      podInfo, err := framework.NewPodInfo(pod)
	      if err != nil {
		      t.Fatal(err)
	      }
	      return podInfo
      }
     ```
     - for non-test files. I simply create an `err` variable to receive the error, and return corresponding function early if this err!=nil.

**Check out the first commit to see which function's return value has changed**
**Check out the second commit to see which function calls have changed has changed**

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

-->
Fixes #112096

#### Special notes for your reviewer:
As far as I know, this change could break `cluster-autoscaler` and the `scheduling-plugins` repo.
I'll open an issue and write the PRs in both repos to adapt to this change.
If there are any other repos affected by this change, please let me know.

issue_context.title: Extract ParseError from PodInfo
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Currently we have `ParseError` here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/891cbede96ab4b64c48edf25f8bbd331d8731622/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L121-L128

And we'll validate the error like this: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/891cbede96ab4b64c48edf25f8bbd331d8731622/pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/interpodaffinity/filtering.go#L243-L246

This is not a golang traditional style, I would like to extract the `ParseError` from `PodInfo`.

The disadvantage is `ParseError` is usually generated in `NewPodInfo`, and `NewPodInfo` is widely used throughout the scheduler.

### Why is this needed?

Make `NewPodInfo` adopt to golang traditional style.

Actually it's not. Although `Cluster Autoscaler` doesn't use `NewPodInfo`, it uses `NewNodeInfo`  which calls `NewPodInfo`. So `NewNodeInfo`  will also have two return values and will cause some code changes in `Cluster Autoscaler`.

`NewPodInfo(pod *v1.Pod) (*PodInfo, error)` 
`NewNodeInfo(pods ...*v1.Pod) (*NodeInfo, error)` 
`(n *NodeInfo) AddPod(pod *v1.Pod) error`

> I found that in some cases,The original code doesn't care if there is an error happened during `NewPodInfo`, [schdule_one](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1913c6be3580da23109493b2bc52b119ee70941e/pkg/scheduler/schedule_one.go#L876) for example. In these cases, the returned podInfo will have correct meta information and some wrong AffinityTerms(`pInfo below`).
> 
> If there is an error occured during `NewPodInfo` now, should I stop the Scheduling process by return a nil podInfo in `NewPodInfo` like this.

I think the intension here is if we parse the affinity terms error, we'll ignore the terms when scheduling. 

See below, if parsing error, the terms will be nil, that means ignore them when scheduling.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/bcea98234f0fdc5ce4e976758977eec72b13bfd4/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L163-L187

> My intension of extracting parseError is that we should explicitly return errors rather than implicitly.

I got it, ignore affinity terms instead of ignoring the pod. Then **how do we deal this error**? Just simply add a log about it?

Currently I ignore the pod when an error occurred in 112219. I'll take some time change the corresponding codes. You can review that pr when I ping you again:)
